title: Adaptive projection ladders reduce reconstruction error without unnecessary explanatory overhead
target: human understanding of a fixed HF01 evidence object

arms.direct: endpoint claim plus endpoint evidence only
arms.fixed_ladder: same content with a fixed set of intermediate representations
arms.adaptive_ladder: intermediate representations inserted/removed based on reconstruction errors

calibration_outcomes: UNKNOWN usage when evidence is insufficient
acceptance: adaptive ladder lowers reconstruction error versus direct projection
adaptive ladder does not require more exposed stages than fixed ladder for equal or better criterion performance
benefit persists on transfer questions rather than verbatim recall
failure_modes: extra stages improve recall but not transfer
extra stages increase confidence without accuracy
adaptive policy overfits to one explanation object
stage count grows without measurable error reduction
stop_rule: Do not add a projection stage unless it reduces a declared reconstruction/calibration error or is required to expose uncertainty/evidence provenance.
claim_boundary: Passing HF-VAL-004 would support an explanation-design strategy. It would not establish that understanding the model changes hair biology.
